title: 2023 AMC 10A Problem 16
statement: In a table tennis tournament every participant played every other participant exactly once. Although there were twice as many right-handed players as left-handed players, the number of games won by left-handed players was \(40\%\) more than the number of games won by right-handed players. (There were no ties and no ambidextrous players.) What is the total number of games played?

solutions.text: Say there are \(L\) left-handers and \(2L\) right-handers, so \(3L\) players and \(\binom{3L}{2}\) games. Every game has one winner, and left wins are \(1.4\) times right wins, so the wins split \(7 : 5\) and the total must be a multiple of \(12\). Left-handers can win at most all games involving at least one left-hander, namely \(\binom{L}{2} + 2L^2\). Hence \[ \frac{7}{12}\binom{3L}{2} \leq \binom{L}{2} + 2L^2, \] which gives \(L \leq 3\). For \(L = 1\) and \(L = 2\), the total is not divisible by \(12\). For \(L = 3\), there are \(\binom{9}{2} = 36\) games. This is attainable if the left-handers win all \(18\) cross-group games and all \(3\) games among themselves, while the right-handers win their \(15\) internal games. The win totals are \(21\) and \(15\), so the answer is \(36\). Therefore, the answer is B.
hints: With \(L\) left-handed and \(2L\) right-handed players, the number of games is \(\binom{3L}{2}\)
Every game has one winner, and left wins to right wins is \(1.4 : 1 = 7 : 5,\) so the total is a multiple of \(12\)
